img_to_keypoints — 2D bridge op

• Data kinds: image → keypoints

• Call: fullseye.apply(img, "img_to_keypoints", a=0.5, b=0.5) (the 2-D model is one image plus two scalar knobs a,b∈[0,1])

*The figure is the actual output on a synthetic 128×128 input. Left: input, right: output. Point clouds are drawn as a top-down scatter (brightness = z), 1-D series as a line plot, volumes as the maximum-intensity projection along z, videos as the middle frame, complex images as magnitude; return values that are not pictures are shown as the values themselves.*

*The 4th column is a colour (H,W,3) input. This op handles colour without crossing channels (it does not convolve the colour channel as a third spatial axis).*

Usage

Turn the local maxima of the image into image-plane points (u, v) = (col, row), shape (N,2).

A pixel is a local maximum if it equals the window maximum from scipy.ndimage.maximum_filter and its value is at or above the threshold (on flat plateaus of equal value every pixel becomes a maximum —— putting gaussian in front reduces this).

• a → side length of the window k = 3 + 2 * int(a * 4) (7 at a=0.5. Larger means sparser).

• b → threshold thr = b (keeps only maxima with value ≥ thr. b=0 keeps every maximum).

• Returns: (N, 2) float64 (u, v) = (col, row). Sorted by descending value, ties in row-major order (deterministic). If not even 1 maximum exists, (0, 2) —— even empty it meets the shape contract, but some downstream ops reject empty input.

• The image border is handled with mode="nearest", so border pixels can also be maxima.

Where to use: entry to tb_keypoints_to_image2d (put the points back into an image) and tb_keypoints_uv_to_points (make a point cloud at z=0).
